newsitem.title: UK: One third of UK consumers will spend windfalls-BRC.
newsitem.headline: One third of UK consumers will spend windfalls-BRC.

text.p: One third of British consumers receiving windfall shares from building society conversions intend to sell them and spend most of the proceeds, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) said on Thursday.

In a survey of over 1,200 consumers who had received or expect to receive windfalls, the BRC found 59 percent intended to hold onto the shares, while 32 percent intended to sell them, with the remaining group unsure of their intentions.
With windfalls set to total 35 billion pounds ($57.2 billion) this year, this represents a spending spree of around 11 billion pounds.
Within the group of consumers eager to cash in their shares, 33 percent intended to spend the money on holidays, 11 percent on cars, and 20 percent on new kitchens, bathrooms or home improvements.
It found 14 percent planned to pay off credit card or other debt while the remaining 17 percent were spending it on the high street, mostly on goods for the home.
But the BRC said this does not represent a windfall-driven buying binge.
"This survey demonstrates what we have been saying all along. People are not going crazy on the high streets," said the BRC's director-general Ann Robinson.
"They are being extremely careful about how they use their money. It is not a surprise that most of the spending is on items that they may have otherwise needed to save for."
